sections.heading: Getting started
paragraphs: Dina was exploring messages and email. The aim was to have a clear, natural conversation in English. Dina said, “I sent you a message yesterday.” A friend replied, “Did you have a chance to read it?” Dina said, “Sorry for the late reply.” A friend replied, “I was away from my phone.” They paused to remember the meaning. Dina said, “I'll reply as soon as I can.” A friend replied, “Could you send me the details?” Dina said, “Please include the date and time.” A friend replied, “I've attached the document.” They paused to remember the meaning. Dina said, “Let me know if the file opens.”

sections.heading: In conversation
paragraphs: The conversation continued, and Dina practiced listening and responding with care. Dina said, “I think the attachment is missing.” A friend replied, “I'll send it again right away.” Dina said, “What should I write in the subject line?” A friend replied, “Keep the subject short and clear.” They paused to remember the meaning. Dina said, “Could you confirm that you received this?” A friend replied, “I received it, thank you.” Dina said, “I will review it this evening.” A friend replied, “Would you prefer email or a text message?” They paused to remember the meaning. Dina said, “Email is easier for longer updates.”

sections.heading: Practicing details
paragraphs: Next, Dina practiced phrases that could help with common problems and decisions. Dina said, “I'll copy the team on the email.” A friend replied, “Please don't share this message publicly.” Dina said, “There was a mistake in my previous email.” A friend replied, “Here is the corrected information.” They paused to remember the meaning. Dina said, “I appreciate your quick response.” A friend replied, “Could you clarify one point?” Dina said, “I want to make sure I understood.” A friend replied, “Let's keep the conversation in one thread.” They paused to remember the meaning.

sections.heading: Putting it together
paragraphs: Before finishing, Dina reviewed more useful sentences and noticed real improvement. Dina said, “I'll follow up tomorrow morning.” A friend replied, “You can reach me here anytime.” Dina said, “I'll turn off notifications tonight.” A friend replied, “I haven't checked my inbox yet.” They paused to remember the meaning. Dina said, “Your message was very helpful.” A friend replied, “I'll save the details for later.” Dina said, “Thanks for keeping me updated.” A friend replied, “Looking forward to hearing from you.” They paused to remember the meaning.
